groups.title: Node IDs drop the file extension (and doc IDs the path), so distinct entities in x.py/x.html or a/x.md/b/x.md collide and one is lost
skill.md: shell injection through `LABELS_DICT` and `INPUT_PATH` in `python -c "..."` blocks, plus three smaller robustness gaps (v0.9.84)

landed.note: Applied to v8 by the maintainer, authorship kept.

4326.summary: A node and its edges now get the same key when graphify runs from a subfolder, so edges stop landing on the wrong node.
4326.why: When graphify starts from a subdirectory of the root, the renamed x.html node got its own id but none of its edges. The cause: by dedup time source_file is already root-relative, but _rank_path still called .resolve(), which prepends the current folder.
4326.what: _rank_path now resolves only absolute paths. Run from root/firmware, the node key is firmware/lib/portal.html, the same as the edge key. The edge lands on firmware_lib_portal_html instead of firmware_lib_portal.
4326.helps: Anyone who runs graphify from a subfolder of the project. Their edges stay on the renamed node. The winner of a collision between relative paths no longer depends on the folder graphify starts from.
4326.diagram:
flowchart LR
  R["run from root/firmware"] --> P["source_file firmware/lib/portal.html"]
  P -- "v8: resolve() adds the CWD" --> B["node key firmware/firmware/lib/portal.html"]:::bad
  B --> BE["edge lands on firmware_lib_portal"]:::bad
  P -- "now: kept as is" --> G["node key firmware/lib/portal.html"]:::good
  G --> GE["edge lands on firmware_lib_portal_html"]:::good
4326.before: Run from root/firmware: node key firmware/firmware/lib/portal.html, edge key firmware/lib/portal.html, edge lands on firmware_lib_portal.
4326.after: Run from root/firmware: node key firmware/lib/portal.html, edge key firmware/lib/portal.html, edge lands on firmware_lib_portal_html.
limits: Does not touch the remaining a/x.md vs b/x.md collision (#4281).
_source_key in extractors/resolution.py is left alone. At extraction time a relative path is still CWD-relative, so resolving it there is right.
A relative path containing .. is no longer normalized in _rank_path. Nodes are relativized before dedup, so stored paths should not contain one.

4371.summary: Reword the id-collision warning so it says what the merge did, instead of claiming a document was lost.
4371.why: The warning claimed that "the dropped node is lost" and that the id "does not identify a single entity", for every such collision. On the reporter's corpus that was wrong: none of their 16 remaining warnings was a lost document. They were one entity described in two documents, or a reference to another file, and merging them was correct.
4371.what: The cross-file branch of the warning now says which node was kept and which was merged into it. The wording then depends on where the id came from: a file path (a reference to the kept file, or a separate document), or neither (probably one entity described in both files). It does not change which node survives. The tests use docs/protocol.md with its own docs_protocol page plus a bare protocol, next to a top-level protocol.md, so this PR and #4410 pass in either merge order (tests/test_dedup.py: 141 passed with both applied).
4371.helps: Whoever reads the collision warning gets text that matches what the merge actually did. The severity stays WARNING.
4371.before: [graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', dropping 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost.
4371.after: [graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files: kept 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', merged 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md' into it. The id comes from neither path, so this is probably one entity described in both files. The merged node's own label and attributes are not kept; its edges stay on the kept node.
limits: The text cannot tell a reference from a second document when the id comes from a path. It says both are possible. Telling them apart needs edge evidence and is out of scope here: #4362 (v0.9.88) and #4410 resolve the cases they can, and this warning covers the collisions they leave, such as docs/protocol.md with its own page that also mints the bare id of a top-level protocol.md.
"Probably one entity" for an id that comes from neither path is an inference, not a fact. Two real documents can also share such an id; the merged node's label and attributes are then lost.
Severity stays WARNING. The reporter asked for something milder, but test_issue_3472 asserts WARNING for a non-path id, so lowering it would change an existing test.
4371.diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["two files mint the same id"] --> Q("where does the id come from?")
  Q -- "a file path" --> Y["warning: a reference to the kept file, or a separate document"]
  Q -- "neither path" --> N["warning: probably one entity described in both files"]
  Y --> S["same node survives as before"]:::same
  N --> S

landed.note: Shipped in v0.9.88. Applied to v8 by the maintainer with an authorship-preserving cherry-pick, so GitHub shows it closed, not merged.

4362.summary: Give each file its own path-qualified id when a dropped folder makes two real documents share a bare id, but keep a reference to another document as one node.
4362.why: Semantic extraction sometimes drops the folder from an id, so a/x.md and b/x.md both emit x. Dedup then merged them and one real document was lost.
4362.what: When files with different paths share a bare id, each file's node is renamed to its path-qualified id (a_x, b_x), unless the bare id is only a mention of another document. A mention is a node that another node of its own file points at with a references edge, and whose id is a shorter path slice of its file. Mentions also lose survivor ties in the collision ranking, so a real document outranks them.
4362.helps: Two real documents with the same bare id stay two nodes instead of one being dropped. A reference to another document no longer becomes a second document or a self-link.
4362.before: a/x.md emits x and b/x.md emits x: dedup keeps one node and b/x.md is dropped (one real document lost).
4362.after: a/x.md emits x and b/x.md emits x: two nodes, a_x and b_x, with edges following their own file.
limits: The mention evidence is inferred from the edges an LLM chose to emit. A missing or reversed references edge gives no evidence, so both files are renamed (R_noedge). With a reversed edge, the reference can still end up as a self-link.
A real document whose own node is linked to its file-level id the same way (an entity named like its file) reads as a mention, and that collision collapses as on v8.
R_toplevel stays wrong: with a top-level protocol.md that also mints protocol, one real document is still dropped by the label tiebreak. It is a separate collision, and a test pins today's result.

If two or more other files also mint the mention's id, the mention stays on the bare id and build_from_json folds it into its own file's page, which gives a self-link and no warning. This is the same outcome as the first version of this PR.
A reference to the bare id from a third file (c.md -> x) cannot be attributed to one file. The edge is left on x, one warning is printed per id, and build() then drops it because no node x exists.

For imports, imports_from and re_exports edges, build_from_json mints an external stub node for the missing target. An import-family edge to a renamed bare id leaves a phantom external node x. Checked by hand; there is no test.

Absolute source_file values (no root, outside the root, or a Windows path on POSIX) are never qualified, so checkout paths cannot leak into ids (#502, #2197, #2618). Those collisions stay on collapse-and-warn.
AST-tier nodes are not touched. Hyperedge members given as dicts are not rewritten, as in the #4282 pass.

cases.correct: 2 nodes; the firmware doc references docs/protocol.md
cases.before: ok, because the mention's label is shorter

cases.correct: no x; c.md's edge not pinned on one file
cases.before: c_note pinned on a_x as EXTRACTED, b/x.md dropped

4362.diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["a/x.md emits id x"] --> Q("both use the bare id x")
  B["b/x.md emits id x"] --> Q
  Q -- "v8" --> V["one node x, b/x.md is lost"]:::bad
  Q -- "this PR" --> P["a_x and b_x, both kept"]:::good
  M["docs/firmware/protocol.md mentions protocol"] --> R("its own file references it")
  R -- "this PR" --> K["stays one node, link ends on docs/protocol.md"]:::good

4353.summary: Stacked on #4344, review that first; its last 4 commits are this PR's own. Step 1 of /graphify now fails loudly when it cannot save its files, and every reader keeps the saved folder name exactly.
4353.why: On a full disk, Step 1 left .graphify_python and .graphify_root empty and still exited 0. The next step then failed with "bash: : command not found", and graphify update rebuilt the current folder instead of the project. Six readers also trimmed spaces from the saved folder, so "proj " came back as "proj".
4353.what: Step 1 writes each file to a temp file and renames it into place. On any error it cleans up, names the file and exits 1. A new read_root_marker() removes only a byte-order mark and a final newline, and graphify update, build.py, watch.py, reflect.py and the git hooks all use it. Step 1 now has both checks: the line-break refusal from #4344 and the loud failure on a failed write from this PR. read_scan_root() from #4344 now calls read_root_marker(), so there is one rule for reading the marker.
4353.helps: Anyone whose disk fills up during Step 1 gets a clear error at that step, not a confusing failure one step later. Anyone with a trailing space in a folder name gets that folder from graphify update.
4353.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Step 1
  participant D as graphify-out
  participant N as Next step
  rect rgba(212, 76, 71, 0.10)
  Note over S,N: Before, with a full disk
  S->>D: write .graphify_python
  D-->>S: write fails, file left empty
  S-->>N: exit 0
  N->>N: bash: : command not found
  end
  rect rgba(68, 131, 97, 0.10)
  Note over S,N: After, with a full disk
  S->>D: write a temp file
  D-->>S: write fails
  S->>D: remove the temp file
  S-->>N: exit 1 and name the file
  end
4353.before: Step 1 with a full disk (ulimit -f 0): exit code 0, .graphify_python and .graphify_root left empty. The next step fails with "bash: : command not found".
4353.after: Step 1 with a full disk: "could not write graphify-out/.graphify_python (File too large; is the disk full?)", exit code 1, no files left behind.
limits: Not tested on Windows PowerShell 5.1. The Windows Step 1 ran under PowerShell 7.4.6 on Linux.
Installed git hooks keep the old code until graphify hook install is run again.
graphify update with an empty .graphify_root now exits 1. A missing .graphify_root still falls back to the current folder.

4344.summary: Skill scripts read the scan folder, community names and spec path from files the agent writes, instead of pasting them into code.
4344.why: The skill told the agent to paste the scan folder, the community names and the spec path into python -c scripts. A value becomes code: a folder named proj$(touch PWNED) ran touch PWNED before Python started, and a label containing a quote could end the Python string early. A scan path that contains a line break could also end the heredoc early (the here-string on PowerShell), and the rest of the path would run as shell. This was reported in a comment on #4309.
4344.what: The agent writes each value to a file in graphify-out/ through a quoted heredoc, and the script reads the file. A new read_scan_root() reads the saved folder. The interpreter path is quoted in every skill script. Step 1 now tells the agent to refuse a scan path with a line break and ask for another one. The Python side rejects multi-line input.
4344.helps: Anyone who runs /graphify on a folder whose name contains shell syntax, or on a path with spaces, no longer runs that name as a command. The scan also stops picking the wrong folder.
4344.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Agent
  participant Sh as Shell
  participant P as Python script
  participant F as graphify-out file
  rect rgba(212, 76, 71, 0.10)
  Note over A,F: Before
  A->>Sh: python -c with the folder name pasted in
  Sh->>Sh: expands proj$(touch PWNED) and runs touch
  Sh->>P: start with the wrong folder
  end
  rect rgba(68, 131, 97, 0.10)
  Note over A,F: After
  A->>F: write the folder name with a quoted heredoc
  A->>Sh: run the script, nothing pasted
  Sh->>P: start
  P->>F: read the folder name as data
  end
4344.before: v8, folder proj$(touch PWNED): the PWNED file is created, then "could not scan .../proj", Detected 0 files.
4344.after: This branch, same folder: nothing is created, Detected 1 files.
limits: Not tested on Windows PowerShell 5.1. The Windows blocks ran under PowerShell 7.4.6 on Linux.
Step 1 leaving empty files on a full disk is a separate bug (#4346), fixed in #4353.
A step run by hand without Step 1 now stops with "graphify-out/.graphify_root not found; run Step 1 first".
The shell ends the heredoc before Python runs, so the agent instruction is the real guard for a path with a line break. The Python check only catches multi-line input that reaches it.
#4353 is stacked on this PR.

4410.summary: Keep docs/protocol.md as its own node when a top-level protocol.md mints the same bare id, and make the real top-level file win the collapse whatever the labels are.
4410.why: When the LLM drops the folder, protocol.md, docs/protocol.md and docs/firmware/protocol.md all mint protocol. #4362 skips any group whose bare id names an input file, because the id may be a reference to that file. The collapse then ran and one real document was dropped. The maintainer named this gap in the review of #4371.
4410.what: The file whose full stem is the id (protocol.md) keeps it and counts toward the collision. Every other file with that bare id is decided on its own: if it has no other node spelled with its own full stem, the bare id is its page and is renamed (docs_protocol); if it has one, the bare id may be a reference and collapses as before. A bare path slice from a file that has its own page now also ranks as a reference, so protocol.md's node survives the collapse whatever the label lengths are.
4410.helps: Anyone with a top-level README or protocol.md next to a docs/ copy of the same name. No document is silently dropped, and a reference to the top-level file lands on it.
4410.before: protocol.md + docs/protocol.md + docs/firmware/protocol.md: nodes docs_protocol, docs_firmware_protocol. protocol.md has no node; the firmware reference ends on docs_protocol.
4410.after: Same input: nodes protocol (protocol.md), docs_protocol, docs_firmware_protocol. The firmware reference ends on protocol.
4410.diagram:
flowchart LR
  B["docs/protocol.md mints protocol"] --> Q("does the file have another node spelled docs_protocol...?")
  Q -- "no: it is the page" --> R["renamed to docs_protocol"]:::good
  Q -- "yes: may be a reference" --> C["collapses onto protocol.md"]:::same
  T["protocol.md mints protocol"] --> K["keeps protocol"]:::good
  C --> K

cases.correct: 2 nodes; the firmware doc references docs/protocol.md

cases.after: ok, the reference lands on protocol.md

cases.correct: no x; c.md's edge not pinned on one file

limits: If the LLM drops the folder AND emits another node spelled with the file's full stem (docs_protocol_header), the file counts as having its own page and gets the collapse it got before. A test pins this.
In R_toplevel one warning still prints: the firmware file's mention of protocol collapses into the top-level node. The merge is right; the warning is noise.
The own-page check reads the nodes the LLM emitted, not the source file.
